prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: [val] Extreme · 10 columns + unbreakable values (language en).
Grid: 10 columns × 4 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "ID" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 16px
  col 2: header "SKU" · longest unbreakable word 44px · one-line width 136px
  col 3: header "Color" · longest unbreakable word 40px · one-line width 40px
  col 4: header "Size" · longest unbreakable word 31px · one-line width 31px
  col 5: header "Qty" · longest unbreakable word 26px · one-line width 26px
  col 6: header "Price" · longest unbreakable word 41px · one-line width 41px
  col 7: header "Tax" · longest unbreakable word 32px · one-line width 32px
  col 8: header "Total" · longest unbreakable word 47px · one-line width 47px
  col 9: header "Warehouse" · longest unbreakable word 81px · one-line width 122px
  col 10: header "Tracking" · longest unbreakable word 159px · one-line width 159px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 720px. You MAY choose a total wider than 719px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Rendering convention: the screenshot always shows the WHOLE table. Anything beyond the dashed box is not clipped; it is the part a reader reaches by scrolling sideways, so judge both what fits in the box at first sight and the cost of scrolling to the rest.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"An order-fulfillment table listing items, quantities, charges, warehouse locations, and shipment tracking.","reading":"Readers scan each row as one item, compare quantities and charges down their columns, and follow the row across to find its warehouse and tracking identifier.","groups":["ID and SKU identify the item; Color and Size describe the variant.","Qty, Price, Tax, and Total form the numeric order and cost group.","Warehouse and Tracking describe fulfillment and shipment."],"keep_intact":["Tracking identifiers and dashes indicating no tracking.","Numeric values and currency amounts.","Color and size values, column headers, and warehouse location codes where possible."],"may_wrap":["SKU codes at natural hyphen breaks.","Warehouse location codes at natural hyphen breaks, while keeping the Warehouse header intact."]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r0A: widths [38, 65, 61, 52, 47, 62, 53, 68, 102, 180] · table 729×355px · row heights [36, 106, 106, 106] · column headers wrapped 0/10 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 9px
Design r0B: widths [38, 65, 61, 52, 47, 62, 53, 68, 102, 172] · table 721×355px · row heights [36, 106, 106, 106] · column headers wrapped 0/10 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 2 · OVERFLOWS the box by 1px
Design r0C: widths [38, 157, 61, 52, 47, 62, 53, 68, 143, 180] · table 862×146px · row heights [36, 36, 36, 36] · column headers wrapped 0/10 · tallest cell 1 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 142px
Constraint adjustments applied: r0A: raised a column to the minimum 38px
r0B: raised a column to the minimum 38px
r0C: raised a column to the minimum 38px

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
